1	# BARITONE-RUNNER.md — `baritone-runner.mjs` operator guide
2	
3	HTTP wrapper around a real (headless-ish) Minecraft Java client driven by
4	Baritone, launched through HeadlessMc. One node process per bot, one HTTP port
5	per bot. Prototype bot: **BariBrute**, port **3301**.
6	
7	Design blueprint lives in `cavecrew-mcp/cave/BARITONE.md`. This file is the
8	*operational* doc for the wrapper: how to run it, what the API is, how the
9	per-instance game directory works, what is pinned, and what it measured.
10	
11	Status: **GREEN — end-to-end verified live 2026-09-01 08:20–08:24 local.**
12	Join, `/status`, `/goto` (two 20-block hops), `/stop`, `/disconnect`,
13	`/shutdown` all confirmed against the real `localhost:25565` server.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## 1. Launch
18	
19	```powershell
20	cd C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter
21	node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 --host localhost --mcport 25565
22	```
23	
24	| flag | default | meaning |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `--name` | `BariBrute` | bot name; also the offline MC username, the `bots\<NAME>\` dir, and the pid file. Hard-capped at 16 chars (MC username limit) — the runner exits if longer. |
27	| `--port` | `3301` | HTTP control port, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. Baritone heavy-lifters own 3301-3309. |
28	| `--host` | `localhost` | MC server host |
29	| `--mcport` | `25565` | MC server port |
30	| `--show-window` | off | leave the real GLFW window visible (debug only; default hides it) |
31	
32	Boot timeline (all of it automatic):
33	
34	```
35	t+0.0s   write bots/<NAME>/HeadlessMC/config.properties  (hmc.gamedir etc.)
36	t+0.0s   preflight: verify java, launcher jar, fabric version, pinned mods
37	t+0.0s   write <gamedir>/baritone/settings.txt  (safety block)
38	t+0.0s   delete stale <gamedir>/logs/latest.log, snapshot pre-existing java PIDs
39	t+0.0s   spawn  java -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar   (cwd = bots/<NAME>)
40	t+4.0s   stdin: launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"
41	t+39.0s  stdin: connect localhost 25565
42	t+51.0s  msg #set chatDebug true ; start position poll
43	```
44	
45	Ready when `GET /status` returns `"phase":"in-world"` and a non-null
46	`position`. Typical wall time from launch to first position: **~55 s**.
47	
48	### The three load-bearing quirks — do not "fix" them
49	
50	1. **No `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's LWJGL redirection layer is incomplete for
51	   1.21.11's RenderPipeline, and the client hangs forever right after the
52	   `minecraft:blur/0` … `blur/5` uniform warnings. We run real LWJGL on the
53	   real GPU and hide the window instead.
54	2. **No `--quickPlayMultiplayer`.** It silently never fires on this HMC/MC
55	   pair — the client sits at the title screen forever with no log trace. The
56	   join is driven manually: after ~35 s, write `connect <host> <port>` to the
57	   launcher's stdin. (`hmc-specifics` `ConnectCommand` reads `args[1]` = host,
58	   `args[2]` = port; a raw space-separated line, no flags.)
59	3. **`-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false` on the CHILD JVM.** `hmc-specifics` mixes
60	   into `Minecraft.<init>` and starts a *second* JLine reader inside the game
61	   process; over the wrapper's plain (non-TTY) pipe it throws
62	   `IllegalStateException: Failed to start JLineCommandLineReader` and kills
63	   the client. The softer `hmc.jline.dumb*` flags do **not** fix this one, and
64	   `config.properties` does not reach the child JVM — it must be on `--jvm`.
65	
66	Never add `-commands`: it conflicts with `hmc-specifics` (maintainer guidance,
67	headlessmc issue #390). `hmc-specifics` alone is the console surface.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 2. HTTP API
72	
73	All endpoints on `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Bodies are JSON. Every command is
74	delivered as a client-side Baritone chat line (`msg #…`) — the `#` prefix is
75	intercepted by Baritone before it leaves for the server, so **nothing this
76	wrapper does produces real server chat, and there is no RCON anywhere.**
77	
78	| method | path | body | action |
79	|---|---|---|---|
80	| GET | `/status` | — | full state (below) |
81	| GET | `/log?tail=N` | — | last N `[CHAT]` lines seen in the client log (ANSI-stripped) |
82	| POST | `/goto` | `{x,y,z}` | FEL no-go gate → `#goto x y z`. 403 if the target is in the box, 400 on non-numeric coords |
83	| POST | `/mine` | `{block,count?}` | `#mine <count> <block>` (Y-clamped by settings.txt) |
84	| POST | `/tunnel` | `{h?,w?,d?}` | refuses (403) if the bot's *current* position is in the no-go box, else `#tunnel h w d` |
85	| POST | `/farm` | `{range?}` | `#farm <range>` |
86	| POST | `/follow` | `{player}` | `#follow <player>` |
87	| POST | `/stop` | — | `#stop`, clears `task` |
88	| POST | `/console` | `{cmd}` | whitelisted read-only Baritone words only: `#eta #proc #goal #version #pause #resume`. 403 otherwise |
89	| POST | `/disconnect` | — | `#stop`, then hmc-specifics `disconnect`; JVM stays up |
90	| POST | `/relog` | — | `disconnect` then `connect` after 3 s; falls back to a full JVM relaunch |
91	| POST | `/shutdown` | — | `#stop` → `disconnect` → kill launcher + client JVM → exit(0) |
92	
93	`GET /status` shape:
94	
95	```json
96	{
97	  "name": "BariBrute",
98	  "position": { "x": 11, "y": 94, "z": 48 },
99	  "positionSource": "goal-poll",
100	  "task": null,
101	  "lastBaritoneLine": "Goal: GoalBlock{x=11,y=94,z=48}",
102	  "connected": true,
103	  "phase": "in-world",
104	  "uptime": 198755,
105	  "joinedAt": 1788243643870,
106	  "aborted": null,
107	  "gameDir": "C:\\Users\\phili\\tools\\baritone-lifter\\bots\\BariBrute\\gamedir",
108	  "launcherPid": 23164
109	}
110	```
111	
112	`phase` walks `starting → launching → connecting → in-world`
113	(`disconnected` / `shutting-down` / `dead` on the way out).
114	`aborted` is `"nogo"` if the position watchdog fired.
115	
116	### How position is obtained
117	
118	There is no protocol client here, so position comes out of the client's own
119	log:
120	
121	- **Idle (no active task): `goal-poll`.** Every 4 s the wrapper sends bare
122	  `#goal`, which sets Baritone's goal to the player's *current* block and
123	  echoes `Goal: GoalBlock{x=…,y=…,z=…}`. Parsed → `position`. Only fired
124	  while idle, because a bare `#goal` during a `#goto` would clobber the goal.
125	- **During a task: `chatDebug`.** `chatDebug true` makes Baritone print
126	  `Starting to search for path from BetterBlockPos{x=…,y=…,z=…} to …`, which
127	  the same parser picks up. Coarser (one fix per path segment), good enough
128	  for the watchdog.
129	
130	Known limitation: during a long `#goto`, position updates only arrive at path
131	re-plan boundaries. If a tighter watchdog is ever needed, the honest fix is a
132	second observer (a mineflayer bot's `/eval` on `bot.players[NAME].entity.position`)
133	rather than polling `#goal` mid-path.
134	
135	### Safety — FEL no-go zone `(-3, 111, 4)` r15 + pad 5
136	
137	Baritone has **no** native coordinate keep-out (upstream #2597, #3847, #1165 —
138	all open, never shipped), so the wrapper enforces it, two layers:
139	
140	- **Layer 1, command gate:** `/goto` rejects any target with
141	  `x ∈ [-23,17] AND z ∈ [-16,24]`, all Y, HTTP 403. `/tunnel` refuses to start
142	  from inside the box. Verified live: `POST /goto {x:-3,y:111,z:4}` →
143	  `403 {"error":"target inside FEL no-go zone"}`.
144	- **Layer 2, position watchdog:** any parsed position inside the box triggers
145	  an immediate `#stop`, clears `task`, and sets `aborted:"nogo"`. This is the
146	  backstop for `#mine`/`#explore`/`#farm` (no coords) and for a legal `#goto`
147	  whose *path* crosses the box — Baritone cannot be told to route around it.
148	
149	**Note the spawn hazard:** the server spawn point `(3.5, 111, -6.5)` is itself
150	inside the padded box. A freshly-spawned bot will trip the watchdog on its
151	first position read. That is correct behaviour, not a bug — walk it out with a
152	gate-approved `/goto` before giving it work.
153	
154	Baritone settings written to `<gamedir>/baritone/settings.txt` on every boot:
155	
156	```
157	legitMine true
158	allowDownward false
159	minYLevelWhileMining -54
160	maxYLevelWhileMining 95
161	blocksToDisallowBreaking chest,trapped_chest,crafting_table,furnace,blast_furnace,oak_sign,oak_wall_sign,barrel
162	chatDebug true
163	```
164	
165	`blocksToDisallowBreaking` takes a **bare comma-separated list, no square
166	brackets**. The bracketed form from the original blueprint makes Baritone
167	1.17.0 log `Unable to parse line … Invalid block name [chest` and silently
168	drop the whole setting — i.e. the protection would look configured but not
169	exist. Fixed and verified: 0 parse errors in the live run.
170	
171	---
172	
173	## 3. Per-instance gameDir — the anti-collision design
174	
175	### The problem
176	
177	HeadlessMc 2.10.0 **ignores the launcher process cwd** when choosing the game
178	directory. Its default is the shared Minecraft install, so every bot got
179	`--gameDir %APPDATA%\.minecraft` and two bots would fight over one
180	`logs/latest.log` (which is the wrapper's entire state wire), one
181	`baritone/settings.txt`, one `options.txt`, one `servers.dat`.
182	
183	### The mechanism (found by decompiling `headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar`)
184	
185	`LauncherProperties.GAME_DIR` → config key **`hmc.gamedir`**.
186	
187	```
188	LauncherProperties:  GAME_DIR = Property("hmc.gamedir")
189	LauncherBuilder   :  config.get(GAME_DIR, <mc install path>) -> FileManager.mkdir(...)
190	ProcessFactory    :  passes it to the child JVM as  --gameDir <path>
191	                     and logs   "Game will run in <path>"     <-- proof line
192	```
193	
194	Sibling key `hmc.game.dir.for.each.version` would append a per-version subdir;
195	the runner pins it to `false` so the path is exactly what we set.
196	
197	It is a **config-file key, not a `launch` flag** — the `launch` command in
198	2.10.0 has no gamedir option (its full flag set is
199	`-id -offline -lwjgl -paulscode -quit -jndi -lookup -commands -inmemory -noout
200	--jvm --retries`; note there is no `--game-args` either, so the old
201	`--game-args "--quickPlayMultiplayer …"` line in the pre-fix runner could
202	never have worked even if quickPlay itself were healthy).
203	
204	HMC's `config.properties` **is** resolved from the launcher's cwd, and the cwd
205	is per bot — so the config file is the isolation lever.
206	`writeHmcConfig()` rewrites it on every boot (merging, not clobbering, any
207	other keys), so `hmc.gamedir` can never drift back to the shared profile.
208	Paths are written with forward slashes because `java.util.Properties` treats
209	`\` as an escape character.
210	
211	### The resulting layout
212	
213	```
214	C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\
215	  baritone-runner.mjs
216	  shared\                                  <- pinned jar library (read-only)
217	  logs\  pids\                             <- wrapper-level
218	  bots\<NAME>\                             <- launcher cwd, PER BOT
219	    headlessmc-launcher.jar
220	    HeadlessMC\config.properties           <- hmc.gamedir, hmc.offline.username
221	    HeadlessMC\<uuid>\                     <- extracted natives (per bot, HMC-side)
222	    HeadlessMC\specifics\hmc-specifics\    <- version-stamped specifics cache
223	    gamedir\                               <- hmc.gamedir target, PER BOT
224	      mods\                                <- the 3 pinned mods
225	      logs\latest.log                      <- STATE WIRE
226	      baritone\settings.txt                <- safety config
227	      baritone\localhost_25565\...\cache   <- baritone world cache
228	      options.txt  saves\  config\  resourcepacks\  data\  downloads\
229	```
230	
231	Deliberately **shared** (content-addressed, no per-session state, ~1 GB):
232	`%APPDATA%\.minecraft\versions\`, `libraries\`, `assets\`. The child JVM still
233	gets `--assetsDir %APPDATA%\.minecraft\assets`. Only runtime state is split.
234	
235	`GAME_DIR` is a pure function of `--name`
236	(`<ROOT>\bots\<NAME>\gamedir`), and `config.properties` is a pure function of
237	cwd (`<ROOT>\bots\<NAME>\HeadlessMC\`), so two runners started with different
238	`--name` values cannot address the same file. Different `--port` values keep
239	the HTTP surfaces apart. Bot #2 can never collide with bot #1.
240	
241	### Verified live (2026-09-01)

243	```
244	[08:17:37] [ProcessFactory]: Game will run in C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\BariBrute\gamedir

257	
258	The shared profile's log and options were not written at any point during the
259	run. Isolation confirmed.
260	
261	### Standing up a second bot
262	
263	```powershell
264	$n = 'BariBonk'   # <= 16 chars, stupid-funny naming law
265	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\$n"
266	Copy-Item C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared\headlessmc-launcher.jar "C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\$n\"
267	node baritone-runner.mjs --name $n --port 3302
268	```
269	
270	The runner creates `gamedir\mods\` and installs the pinned mods from `shared\`
271	itself. **Only run a second bot after checking the RAM budget in §5 — the law
272	is max 2 baritone clients alongside the 8-bot mineflayer fleet.**
273	
274	---
275	
276	## 4. Pinned versions
277	
278	Nothing in `baritone-runner.mjs` resolves a "latest" URL or tag, and the
279	runner never downloads. `preflight()` verifies every pinned artifact exists on
280	disk and **exits non-zero with a list** rather than fetching a substitute. It
281	also refuses to boot if the per-instance `mods\` contains any jar that is not
282	on the pinned list, which is what catches version drift.
283	
284	| component | version | file / path |
285	|---|---|---|
286	| Java | 21.0.10 | `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe` |
287	| HeadlessMc launcher | 2.10.0 | `bots\<NAME>\headlessmc-launcher.jar` (copy of `shared\headlessmc-launcher.jar`) |
288	| Minecraft | 1.21.11 | `%APPDATA%\.minecraft\versions\1.21.11\` |
289	| Fabric loader | 0.19.3 | version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11` |
290	| Fabric API | 0.141.6+1.21.11 | `shared\fabric-api-0.141.6+1.21.11.jar` |
291	| Baritone | 1.17.0 | `shared\baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` (cabaletta official, built for 1.21.11) |
292	| hmc-specifics | 2.4.0 | `shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar` |
293	
294	Launcher version selector is `fabric:1.21.11`, which HMC matches against the
295	installed version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11`. That is the only fabric
296	version installed, so the selector is unambiguous — not a floating "latest".
297	
298	**Do not use `shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar`.** It is the
299	same bytes but under the upstream "-latest" download name. HMC itself installs
300	the version-stamped `hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar` into
301	`<gamedir>\mods\`; having both names present makes Fabric abort with a
302	duplicate-mod error. The `-latest` copy is kept only as the original download
303	receipt. `preflight()` will refuse to boot if it ever lands in a mods dir.
304

while true; do
  NOW=$(date +%s); ELAPSED=$((NOW-START))
  if [ $ELAPSED -ge 1500 ]; then
    echo "CAP: 25min elapsed t+${ELAPSED}s -- stopping watch loop, driver must /stop and wrap up"
    break
  fi
  STATUS=$(curl -s --max-time 8 http://127.0.0.1:3301/status)
  if [ -z "$STATUS" ]; then
    echo "ALERT NOSTATUS t+${ELAPSED}s -- wrapper /status unreachable"
  else
    CONN=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"connected":[a-z]*')
    ABORTED=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"aborted":"[a-zA-Z]*"')
    TASK=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"task":null')
    LASTLINE=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"lastBaritoneLine":"[^"]*"')
    if echo "$ABORTED" | grep -q nogo; then
      echo "ALERT NOGO_WATCHDOG_FIRED t+${ELAPSED}s -- $STATUS"
    fi
    if echo "$CONN" | grep -q false; then
      echo "ALERT DISCONNECTED t+${ELAPSED}s -- $STATUS"
    fi
    if [ -n "$TASK" ] && [ $ELAPSED -gt 15 ]; then
      echo "TASKCLEARED t+${ELAPSED}s -- baritone task went idle on its own (mine finished or errored) -- $STATUS"
    fi
  fi
  ITER=$((ITER+1))
  if [ $((ITER % 3)) -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "hb t+${ELAPSED}s $LASTLINE"
  fi
  if [ $((ITER % 6)) -eq 0 ]; then
    GT=$(curl -s --max-time 8 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"code":"return bot.players[\"BariBrute\"]?.entity?.position ?? null"}')
    echo "groundtruth t+${ELAPSED}s $GT"
  fi
  sleep 20
done
echo "WATCHLOOP_DONE t+${ELAPSED}s"

START=$(date +%s)
ITER=0
while true; do
  NOW=$(date +%s); ELAPSED=$((NOW-START))
  if [ $ELAPSED -ge 400 ]; then
    echo "CAP: return-watch window elapsed t+${ELAPSED}s -- check /status manually"
    break
  fi
  STATUS=$(curl -s --max-time 8 http://127.0.0.1:3301/status)
  if [ -z "$STATUS" ]; then
    echo "ALERT NOSTATUS t+${ELAPSED}s"
  else
    CONN=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"connected":[a-z]*')
    ABORTED=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"aborted":"[a-zA-Z]*"')
    TASK=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"task":null')
    LASTLINE=$(echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"lastBaritoneLine":"[^"]*"')
    if echo "$ABORTED" | grep -q nogo; then
      echo "ALERT NOGO_WATCHDOG_FIRED t+${ELAPSED}s -- $STATUS"
    fi
    if echo "$CONN" | grep -q false; then
      echo "ALERT DISCONNECTED t+${ELAPSED}s -- $STATUS"
    fi
    if [ -n "$TASK" ] && [ $ELAPSED -gt 10 ]; then
      echo "ARRIVED: task cleared on its own t+${ELAPSED}s -- $STATUS"
      break
    fi
  fi
  ITER=$((ITER+1))
  if [ $((ITER % 2)) -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "hb t+${ELAPSED}s $LASTLINE"
  fi
  sleep 15
done
echo "RETURNWATCH_DONE t+${ELAPSED}s"

## [open] genuinely undug rock corridor near cluster 3 → mineBlocks/buildStaircase both false-reach loop instead of digging through → real drowning incident — Thak, 2026-09-01
Cluster 3 (23-24,y46-47,77-79) sits 4-5 blocks past a wall of SOLID, NEVER-DUG stone from the
